rv.q: Superbly directed by Diane Paulus, with a stellar octet of players headed by John Turturro and Paul Giamatti
Tony Award-winning director Diane Paulus and her star-studded cast will mesmerize you with the most energetic, innovative, talented and — yes — hilarious evening of theater this side of Broadway.
It deserves to be seen by an even larger audience, and here's hoping it makes its way to a New York City stage soon.
Rightly so, it's a grand production worthy of its hype.
The pacing issue is noticeable, but it does not overshadow a production that clearly understands what it wants its audience to take away.

The A.R.T. has tinkered with the long-standard English translation by Derek Prouse, cutting some minor characters and streamlining scenes, but they’ve thankfully resisted the temptation to overplay any correlations to current movements or people — no orange wigs or red hats on the rhinos — in part because they don’t have to.
The anti-totalitarian core is sure to strike a chord in the current political and social context of the United States.
Fortunately, the actors were usually able to bring the energy back with a sharp joke, quick exchange, or burst of physical comedy.

cn.t: ART's "Rhinoceros" proves startlingly prescient, with Paulus's direction and a stellar cast (Giamatti, Turturro, Maslany) delivering absurdist hilarity in act one before turning bone-chilling. Dialogue-heavy pacing occasionally drags, but the production feels urgently timely.
